analysis.evidence: Abram is the subject. בָּאָרֶץ identifies the land he passed through, and עַד מְקוֹם שְׁכֶם marks how far he went, as far as Shechem.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed conjunction וַ with a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, agreeing with אַבְרָם.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּעֲבֹר אַבְרָם בָּאָרֶץ, אַבְרָם names the subject of וַיַּעֲבֹר, “Abram passed through the land.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name without a prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68128:9, 68104:8, 67089:19, 67078:6, 67077:6, 66574:12.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, singular absolute, common gender, with prefixed בְּ and the definite article.

analysis.evidence: וַיַּעֲבֹר אַבְרָם בָּאָרֶץ describes Abram traveling through the land. עַד מְקוֹם שְׁכֶם identifies the place he reached.
analysis.morphology: A preposition with no prefix or suffix. Its complement is מְקוֹם שְׁכֶם, “the place of Shechem.”
analysis.sense: as far as, up to, to (a place or person)

analysis.evidence: עַד מְקוֹם שְׁכֶם means “as far as the site of Shechem.” The name שְׁכֶם identifies the place Abram reached.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, directly preceding the place name שְׁכֶם.

analysis.evidence: In עַד מְקוֹם שְׁכֶם, “as far as the site of Shechem,” שְׁכֶם names the place Abram reached. The following עַד אֵלוֹן מוֹרֶה, “as far as the oak of Moreh,” identifies the local landmark.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun used as a place name, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The second עַד introduces אֵלוֹן מוֹרֶה, the oak of Moreh. It specifies more precisely where Abram went after the verse names the place of Shechem.
analysis.morphology: Simple preposition with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: as far as, up to, to (a place or person)

analysis.evidence: The repeated עַד locates Abram first at Shechem and then more precisely at אֵלוֹן מוֹרֶה, “the terebinth of Moreh.” The construct phrase identifies the tree as a landmark.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state before מוֹרֶה, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: A great tree or terebinth serving as a landmark.

analysis.evidence: In וְהַכְּנַעֲנִי אָז בָּאָרֶץ, ‘and the Canaanites were then in the land,’ the definite singular names the people living in the land through which Abram passed.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ ‘and’ and definite article הַ ‘the’ precede a masculine singular absolute gentilic used collectively.
